ov: A big cat of the high mountains of Central and South Asia, slightly smaller than the other big cats in its genus. Its thick whitish-grey fur has black spots and rosettes, and it lives alone at 3,000–4,500 m, among cliffs and ridges.

why.dg: Only three attacks on people have ever been reported, and none was fatal.

len: 75–150 cm head and body, plus an 80–105 cm tail
ht: Up to 56 cm at the shoulder
rg: Mountains of Asia, from the Hindu Kush, Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau to southern Siberia, Mongolia and western China.
df: Wild hoofed animals, and domestic livestock.
fx: Fewer than 10,000 mature snow leopards are thought to be left in the wild.
Its fur hairs are 5–12 cm long, and its broad paws and thick tail suit it to cold mountains.
